summaryTr: Sermet Bey, kalabalık ailesi için kiraladığı ve perili olduğu söylenen beyaz köşke taşınır; gözüyle gördüğüne değil, eliyle dokunduğuna inanan bu adam her gece görünen hayaletin peşine düşer. Ömer Seyfettin'in mizahlı hikâyesinin A2 seviyesinde, sade bir İngilizce uyarlaması.
paragraphs: ## A White House for Rent

Sermet Bey stopped and turned to the old watchman behind him. The old man was showing him empty houses in the neighbourhood, because Sermet Bey needed a big home for his family. "Look," he said. "Here is one more empty house."

In front of a small pine wood stood a smart white house. It shone in the sun like marble, so brightly that it hurt the eyes. Wild grass was growing in its flower beds. A big sign hung on the iron gate of the garden. It said: FOR RENT.
The watchman shook his head. "Go on, sir, go on! That house is not for you."
"Why not, my friend?"
"Take the house I showed you a moment ago. It is small, but it is very lucky. A boy is born to every family that lives there."
"How can twelve people live in five rooms?" said Sermet Bey. "Let us look at this one. It is just right for us."

Sermet Bey could not take his eyes off the house. It had wide balconies on every side, and it sat low and wide on its stone base, like a white hen on her eggs. For twenty years, since his children were born, he always dreamed of a nest like this for his family. "Why can't we live here?" he asked quickly.
"Because there is a ghost in this house, sir."
"What ghost?"
"A real ghost! It comes out at night. It doesn't let the people inside rest."

Sermet Bey was not a man who believed everything he saw or heard. He believed in a thing only when he could touch it and hold it tightly in his hand. For him, the eyes and the ears were full of lies. Every lie came into our heads through these four doors: two eyes and two ears. But the hand was different. The hand never believed a lie. So Sermet Bey only laughed.
"A ghost will not hurt us," he said.
The watchman looked at him as if Sermet Bey had said a bad word. "Everybody says that at first, sir. But nobody stays here for a month."
"That is not your business. Let us see the inside."
"The key is with the owner, sir. He is Hacı Niyazi Efendi, and he lives in the old red house near here."
"Then let us get the key."

They turned back and walked towards an old house painted red, between thick trees. On the way the watchman told Sermet Bey the story of the white house. For ten years, nobody who rented it stayed more than a month. First the ghost showed itself. Then it threw big stones. At last it broke the windows, and the family inside could not sleep at night. Two tenants nearly died of fear. In three families a child became very sick. One man's wife was so afraid that she lost her baby before it was born.
They passed under flowering almond trees and knocked on the green door of the red house.
## Three Years in Advance

Hacı Niyazi Efendi was an old government clerk. He left his office some years ago, and since then he made his living by buying and selling houses. But he was an honest man. He sold perhaps a hundred houses a year, and yet he never sold his own haunted house to a stranger who knew nothing about the place. "I fear God," he always said. "I don't want trouble." He never hid the secret of his mansion.
He opened the door himself. The watchman said that Sermet Bey wanted to see the white house. "Very well, please come," said the old man.

He walked in front of them through his garden. In the street he took a brass key out of the pocket of his yellow coat and opened the gate of the white house. "This key opens the mansion too," he said to Sermet Bey.

They went in. The garden was really quite wild. Nobody looked after it, and it looked like the bed of a dry stream. At the back, in the small pine wood, there was a strange silence. The watchman did not come into the house. He stayed at the door. Sermet Bey walked through the rooms with the owner. The decoration was perfect. The whole ground floor was marble. There was a water tank, a bathroom, a well, a chicken house and a stable. Everything was complete.
"How much is the rent?" asked Sermet Bey.
"I don't ask for much. One hundred and eighty lira a year. But I want three years in advance."
"Why?"

"I will tell you why, sir. My enemies started this talk about a ghost, so that my house stays empty. When somebody rents it, everybody in the street begins to talk about the ghost, and they do it for nothing! In the end the tenants think that the lies they heard are things they saw. In the middle of winter they leave the house and run away, and I have no tenant and no rent. And it is worse than that: when they leave, they join the talkers."
"Do people leave quickly?"
"People listen to the neighbours. They get afraid and run away."
"I will not get afraid."
"God willing."
"But three years in advance is a little heavy for me."
"What can I do, sir? I have lost too much already. If you like..."
Sermet Bey liked the mansion very much, and the rent was cheap. People were asking one hundred and fifty lira a year for a little house with three rooms.

They signed a contract that same day. The rent for three years, five hundred and forty lira, was to be paid at once. When they came out of Hacı Niyazi Efendi's house, Sermet Bey took out a banknote and gave it to the watchman as a present.
"That money is wasted, sir," said the watchman. "You will not stay three years. You will not stay three months."
"You will see."
"We will see. Hacı Efendi takes three years in advance from everyone like this. But not one of them stayed through a summer. They all lost their money."
## The White Shape in the Pines

A week later Sermet Bey moved into the mansion with his big family. He loved pleasure. Every night there was music, a big dinner and fun, and there were always four or five guests from the family. Sermet Bey was a Turk, but he liked a European rule: "Hard work by day, pleasure by night."

In the daytime the family was busy. The children went to school, his daughters worked as clerks in big offices, and his wife gave piano lessons. Only his mother, who was seventy-five, stayed at home and looked after the kitchen and the servants. They ate dinner almost at midnight and went straight to bed.

Less than two weeks passed. One night there was a scream from the ground floor. The servant, Artemisya, ran upstairs, shouting at the top of her voice. She said she had seen something white walking about among the pines behind the house.
"You imagined it!" said Sermet Bey.

Then all of them, parents and children, went out onto the balcony of the back room. Artemisya pointed with her finger. There it was: a white ghost, standing under the trees. It seemed to look at the mansion. Sermet Bey rubbed his eyes.
"Well, well!" he said. "Look at the power of an idea!"
His wife, his daughters and the children turned pale with fear. His eldest daughter said, "What idea, Father? It is there, in front of us. Don't you see it?"
"I see it."
"Then what are you talking about?"
"Since we came to this house, what have we heard? Nothing but ghost stories. Everybody told us something. Now, because of that, all of us together see a thing that is not there."
"That is not possible."
"Why not?"

Sermet Bey told them about Kazanov, a magician who made a whole theatre full of people read the wrong time on their watches. "Our eyes see the lies that come in through our ears," he said. "But we do not touch the thing we see. If we touch it, it disappears at once."

Then he got up. His wife told him not to go, but he did not listen. He ran out into the garden to touch the white shape with his own hand. He went towards the pines. But the shape ran away and was gone. That night nobody in the house could sleep, except Sermet Bey.

After that, they saw the white shape every night. When Sermet Bey went out to touch it, it always ran away. Slowly the family began to get used to it. But one night, while they were all sleeping, the whole house shook with a terrible bang. They ran to the balconies, but they saw nothing. In the morning they found a huge stone by the wall of the dining room.

Sermet Bey's mother began to say, "If you don't take us out of this house, I will never forgive you." Two months in a house that cost five hundred and forty lira! But every night more big stones fell, and the family could not sleep. The neighbours heard about the stones and said, "If you don't leave, it is going to break your windows too."

Sermet Bey remembered a line in the contract: "When the tenant leaves, he pays for all repairs." This worried him more. He wanted to do something before the window-breaking time came. Slowly, even his own belief began to shake. At last the family decided to leave. But they could not find another house. And now they began to hear a thousand more stories about the mansion. Some people said it was a graveyard long ago. Others said that a holy man from five hundred years ago was lying under the kitchen.

But in spite of the stones and the broken windows, Sermet Bey still did not believe in the ghost. This ghost always ran into the pine wood and disappeared there. One day Sermet Bey had an idea. He could hide in the pine wood and jump out in front of the ghost. Or he could follow it quietly and touch it from behind. Nobody in his family agreed. "It will strike you dead on the spot!" they said. But Sermet Bey, although he felt a little sick with worry, did not believe in spirits or in any such thing.

The next evening he went to the pine wood. He climbed onto the low branches of a big pine tree and waited. He waited and waited. It became midnight. The people in the mansion could not sleep either, because they were so curious. He could see the poor things walking up and down on the balconies. Suddenly his heart jumped. The white shape had come out.
## A Hand on the Ghost

Sermet Bey knew for sure that his hand would go through the shape like a shadow. Even so, his knees began to shake. "I am not afraid," he said to himself, "but my body is afraid!" Quietly he jumped down from the tree and walked after the white shape. The ghost did not hear him coming. Slowly he put out his hand and touched the white body.
The shape was terribly frightened. But it did not disappear. It turned, saw Sermet Bey, and began to run as fast as it could.

Sermet Bey understood at once that this was no ghost, because it did not disappear when he touched it. He did not let it go. He chased it. At the end of the pine wood there was a low wall, and a plank was leaning against it. The shape was climbing the plank when he caught it. Sermet Bey was very strong. When the shape saw that it could not win, it stopped fighting.
"I am going to show you how to make fun of people!" said Sermet Bey. He took hold of the poor ghost and dragged it towards the house. "Bring a lamp!" he shouted. "Let us see its face!"
The whole household came down to the garden gate.
"It is a human being, the rascal!" said Sermet Bey. "Didn't I always say that there are no ghosts in this world?"

The ghost did not want to let go of the white sheet on its head. Sermet Bey pulled it off by force. Then everybody was surprised. Under the sheet was Hacı Niyazi Efendi, with his beard and moustache all mixed up! The poor man covered his face with his hands. His fine nightgown was torn at the back.
Sermet Bey burst out laughing. The girls, the children and the servants stood with their mouths open. Sermet Bey's old mother said, "Why do you frighten people and drive them mad, sir?"
"I know the reason for that!" answered Sermet Bey.

Then he told his eldest daughter to bring pen and ink and the contract from the desk, quickly. Hacı Niyazi Efendi stood like a frozen man. He did not answer any question. He only kept turning his face to the dark. When the paper and the pen came, Sermet Bey said, "Come on, take the pen! If you don't want to be punished for the people you frightened, and for the baby that was lost, write what I say and sign it!"
Hacı Niyazi Efendi took the pen like a machine. Without waiting, he wrote down, word by word, what Sermet Bey said:
"I have received from my tenant Sermet Bey one thousand and eighty lira in advance, the rent of the mansion for six years."
"That's it!" said Sermet Bey.

Hacı Niyazi Efendi signed his name. The paper said that Sermet Bey had already paid for six years, but he had paid for only three. So Sermet Bey got three more years in the mansion, and he did not pay for them. Then the owner, half wrapped in his white sheet again, went away to the place where the ghost disappeared every night.

Two years later, everybody was amazed that Sermet Bey still lived in the mansion. The neighbours said to Hacı Niyazi Efendi, "It seems that the ghosts of your house have gone to another house. Your new tenant does not look like leaving!"

Each time he heard this, he first turned pale, then red, and he muttered the same answer: "No prayers, no fasting! Men and women, parents and children, all of them are drunk from evening until morning! My dear sir, not even a ghost can frighten such people. Even the devil cannot show his face to them!"

glossary.bey: Bey (Türkçede adın sonuna gelen saygı unvanı, 'Bay' gibi)
glossary.bed: yatak (dry stream bed = kurumuş dere yatağı)

phrases.tr: (look after) bakmak, ilgilenmek, göz kulak olmak

options: Everything that the neighbours said
Everything that he heard
Only the things that he could touch
Only the things that he saw at night
quiz.explainTr: Sermet Bey'e göre göz ve kulak yalanla doludur; o yalnızca eliyle dokunup tutabildiği şeye inanır.

quiz.q: Why did Hacı Niyazi Efendi want three years of rent in advance?
options: Because the house was very big
Because tenants always ran away and left him with nothing
Because he wanted to buy a new house
Because Sermet Bey was a rich man
quiz.explainTr: Ev sahibi, kiracıların hayalet lafına kapılıp kış ortasında kaçtığını, bu yüzden kirayı peşin istediğini söyler.

quiz.q: What did Sermet Bey do when the family saw the white shape from the balcony?
options: He called the watchman
He hid in his room
He told his mother to pray
He ran into the garden to touch it
quiz.explainTr: Sermet Bey, bunun yalnızca bir telkin olduğunu söyler ve eliyle dokunmak için bahçeye koşar; ama hayal kaçar.

options: The owner of the house
The old watchman
A holy man from the graveyard
One of the servants
quiz.explainTr: Hayalet, çarşafa bürünmüş ev sahibi Hacı Niyazi Efendi'ydi; kiracıları korkutup kaçırıyor, peşin kirayı cebine atıyordu.

quiz.q: How did the story end for Sermet Bey?
options: He left the mansion after three months
He paid for six more years of rent
He got three more years in the mansion without paying
He had to repair all the broken windows
quiz.explainTr: Sermet Bey, ev sahibine altı yıllık kirayı peşin aldığına dair bir belge imzalattı; böylece üç yıl daha bedava oturdu.
